children.text: 按玩家顺序，每名调查员选择下列适用于自己的梦境条目之一，并大声朗读。「中立」梦境可由任何调查员选择。若有可能，每名调查员必须选择不同的梦境。然后，前往〈设置〉。

守卫者（[guardian]）之梦：你绕着一座阴郁的小山打转，那山被黑暗笼罩、浸在浓雾之中，仿佛把一切声音都吞了进去。你不知道山丘里安息着什么，只觉得它比这个世界更古老，而且似乎正在注视着你。你不敢转身面朝那座坟丘，却知道自己离不开它，于是只好无休止地绕着它巡守。在周围的树篱间，你瞥见扭曲的影子来回窜动，可每当你的火把照过去，它们就消失了。你开始奔跑，却被身后一声巨响钉在原地。当你转过身，雾气散开，你终于看见山丘的底部——那里有一扇厚重的、风化的石板门在呼唤你。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张守卫者（[guardian]）卡并打出（支付其费用）。
探求者（[seeker]）之梦：你匆匆穿过一所几乎认不出来的大学的走廊，怀里抱着几本教科书，快步从其他学生和教职员身边经过。你不知道自己怎么会忘记考试的日期，但你知道，若不能及时赶到，这门课就会挂掉。不知为何，你甚至连课程的主题和教学内容都不记得了，尽管你清楚这已是学期末。逃课或忘记温习可不是你的作风。你经过时，能听见其他学生在偷笑。走到走廊尽头，教室的门阴沉沉地压在你面前。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张探求者（[seeker]）卡并打出（支付其费用）。

流浪者（[rogue]）之梦：你端详自己的牌，暗暗藏住笑意。方块 J、黑桃 Q，正好凑成一手无可超越的顺子。你的筹码每局都在变多，这一局也不会例外。赌注你来我往，直到桌边只剩你和对面那个穿白西装的男人。「你确定要这样？」他一边把玩手指一边挑衅。你把所有筹码推进桌心，亮出你的 K 高顺子。「真可惜。」他啧啧出声，亮出一对 2。「看来你把一切都输光了。」你出言抗议，指着自己更大的牌型，可当你再看那手牌时，它已经变了。人头牌上的图案如今是没有眼睛、生着许多张嘴和触手手臂的怪物形状。「9♥-10♣-D♦-C♠-N（自动失败）」牌上这样写着。你惊得张口结舌，被人从牌桌旁架起，推出了门外。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张流浪者（[rogue]）卡并打出（支付其费用）。

神秘学家（[mystic]）之梦：你走过一条充满色彩与生机的魔幻小路。光点在空气中悬着，随着你的靠近上下浮动。你每迈出一步，路旁的植物便违背一切自然法则地枯萎下去。曾经在你身后绽放的花朵，如今在你经过时蜷缩；藤蔓枯萎死去。那些光点嘲笑你的无知，你却没有放慢脚步。当你望向那些秀美的树木，树叶开始飘落。曾经翠绿的草变得干枯、褐黄、龟裂。但纵然整座森林都死去，能抵达另一边也是值得的。当你终于抵达时，小径戛然而止——眼前是一扇雕刻在巨大红杉树干上的华美木门。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张神秘学家（[mystic]）卡并打出（支付其费用）。
幸存者（[survivor]）之梦：你在一条阴暗狭窄、木墙上爬满藤蔓的走廊中奔逃。有什么难以解释的东西在昏暗中追赶你。你怕得不敢回头去看追赶者，但你清楚，一旦它抓住你，你的命就到此为止。它会刺穿你的心脏、抽干你的血、吞食你的内脏。正是这个念头催你向前，让你跑得比以往任何时候都快。你不能让它碰到你。你不能让它进食。忽然，你看见了出路：一扇结实的木门，四周围着一堵藤蔓墙。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张幸存者（[survivor]）卡并打出（支付其费用）。

罪犯之梦：警笛的尖啸在你身后的街道上回荡。他们正在逼近。他们一直紧咬着你的脚跟，而你总能快他们一步……直到现在。你跑进一条小巷，一道鲜红的光跟着你。他们要抓住你了。他们会把你锁进笼子，再把钥匙扔掉。你的自由、你的生活方式、你的一切、你所爱的一切：他们要把这些统统夺走。凭什么？就因为你不肯照他们的规矩来？他们什么时候把所有事都弄对过？就在警察快要追上你的时候，你转过一个街角，看见一栋砖砌建筑的入口。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张罪犯或非法卡并打出（支付其费用）。

漂泊者之梦：你在花田中漫步，和煦的春风推着你的脚步向前。一条铁轨把花田一分为二，当你走到那两条平行的钢线前，蒸汽与钢铁的轰鸣朝你碾压而来。列车驶过时，你抓住其中一节锈迹斑斑、饱经风霜的车厢上垂下的梯子。尽管外表如此，车厢内部却处处是意想不到的奢华与富丽：波斯地毯挂在墙上作装饰，大理石楼梯盘旋到令人眩晕的高处，水晶吊灯把棱彩的碎光洒满整个房间。吊灯下方立着一扇华美的门，镀金的格栅拼成林间一只狐狸的图案。
你可以将牌库中的 1 张基础弱点替换为另一张随机基础弱点。若你如此做，承受 1 点由你选择的创伤。

猎人之梦：你在一栋破败的宅子里潜行追踪猎物，走廊里满是霉味与尘土。你追猎的生物来自一个非自然的世界，是令人憎恶的存在。它仅凭自身的存在就威胁着人类的存亡。你瞥见它那诡异的身影走进楼上的一扇门。它现在逃不掉了——它是你的了。可当你走进它的巢穴，却只找到一面肮脏、开裂的镜子，镜中映出你自己疲惫而忧虑的脸。那畸变之物能逃到哪里去？你确定它退进了这里，然而……你转身回到入口，惊讶地发现原先没有门的地方多了一扇门。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张武器卡并打出（支付其费用）。

医生或助手之梦：你站在一具合上的棺木前。身着黑衣的哀悼者在你身旁排成一列，等着你说最后的悼词。你含着泪把手放在棺木上。那坚硬冰冷的木头在掌心下毫无生气。他们曾向你倾诉，他们曾依靠你。而在他们最需要的时候，你辜负了他们。这一切——冰冷的棺木、哀痛的亲友——全都是因为你。可当你打开棺木，里面没有尸体：只有一条长长的石砌通道，通向地底深处。突然，一名哀悼者从背后推了你一把，你越过棺木边缘跌进下方的坑中，侧身落地，疼得厉害。当你站起身来，你发现唯一的出口是一座石拱门，它通向完全不同的某个地方……
选择另一名调查员。该调查员以多 2 点资源和多 1 张起始手牌开始本剧本。

密斯卡托尼克或学者之梦：你身处一座古老而被遗忘的藏书室，四周是先贤的知识。成十万计的典籍排满书架，向上延伸进一片空无的虚空。昏暗的厅堂里弥漫着陈旧书页与融蜡的气味。你从旁边的书架上取下一本厚重的典籍，开始阅读。虽然你似乎读不懂其中任何一个字，却完全被书页编织的故事吸住了。随着时间流逝，周围的一切都淡成琐碎之物。除了那深红墨迹的形状，什么都不重要；面对如此赤裸的真相，其余一切都没有意义。在你四周，藏书室正烧向地基。就在火焰烧到你身上时，一扇离开藏书室的门在呼唤你。不知怎的，它竟在烈焰中未被烧毁。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张典籍卡并打出（支付其费用）。
老兵之梦：你身处一条泥泞、满是煤灰的战壕。四周，战争那雷鸣般的喧嚣一波波涌来，永无休止。战壕里横陈着死者：那些在远离家乡的土地上、为了一场虚无而丢掉性命的友人与战友。你越过战壕边缘望向无人区——一片破碎焦黑的荒芜之地，踏进去必死无疑。就在那里，你看见了它：一扇孤零零的木门立在瓦砾与泥土之间。你知道那是你唯一的出路。你紧紧握住步枪，翻出战壕，一头冲进致命的弹雨，爆炸在你身边摇动大地。
从你的牌库中搜寻至多 2 张战术和/或补给卡，并以这些卡作为起始手牌的额外卡牌开始本剧本。

旅人之梦：你在齐胸深的咸水沼泽中艰难跋涉。大得不可能的芦苇高耸在你头顶，成群奇异、泛着虹彩的昆虫在恶臭的空气中飞绕。你每走一步，双脚就陷进更深的软泥，仿佛要把你拖到水底。你感到有什么滑腻冰冷的东西滑过你的腿，便朝干地扑去——可你越是挣扎，就陷得越远。眨眼之间，你整个人被泥沼吞没，却仍在不断向下坠落。最后，你随着一小股泥流被抛到石砌的地面上。你发现自己身处一间封闭的墓室，奇异的象形文字泛着淡蓝的微光，照亮四周。那些符号框出一扇精巧的金色大门：正是你一直在寻找的那座地穴之门。
从你的牌库中搜寻 1 张旅人或遗物卡并打出（支付其费用）。
中立之梦：你翻来覆去，却一刻也没有真正睡着。你的脑中塞满不适与阴郁的念头：失败的念头、无能的念头、失去的念头。你满头是汗。无论怎么躺，床不是太热就是太冷。终于，你受够了这种徒劳，起身走到水槽边往脸上泼了些水。就在这时你才发现，房间的布局已不是原来的样子——而通往浴室的门被换成了一座巨大的缟玛瑙与大理石大门。
你以多 2 点资源开始本剧本。

中立之梦：你坐在似乎是童年故居的后院露台上，但有什么不对劲。你认不出自己的家人……后院的植物摆得不一样了……天空则成了腐烂尸体的拼贴，断肢残躯如雨般落向大地。你那并非家人的家人平静地看着这场尸雨，像谈论一件乏味小事一样议论着天气。即便落到屋顶上的手脚拍击声愈发密集、变成让天花板下陷的残躯洪流，他们依旧如此。你跑到屋外，在致命的雨幕中穿行，本能地朝父母家宅地的边缘走去。身后传来房屋坍塌的巨响，你扒开堆在一处熟悉旧地上的断肢，如释重负地摸到那扇风化木制的地窖门。
你以多 1 张起始手牌开始本剧本。
从以下遭遇组中收集所有卡牌：梦境门外、奈亚拉托提普的使徒、祖格鼠、入梦者的诅咒、幻梦境与刺骨严寒。
将七十级台阶（浅眠）与火焰洞穴置入游戏。每名调查员从七十级台阶（浅眠）开始。
将以下卡牌放在一边、移出游戏：伦道夫·卡特（资深入梦者）、辛劳的古革巨人敌人、两张双面的敌人卡（纳什特与卡曼塔），以及其余所有地点。
注意：纳什特与卡曼塔是双面卡，它们的另一面是剧情卡。为获得最佳体验，除非有某个效果指示你这么做，否则不要查看另一面。
本剧本开始时，游戏中没有遭遇牌库。将剩余的所有遭遇卡堆成一叠，放在一边。稍后会把它们一起洗混，组成遭遇牌库。（见下文「沉眠阶梯」。）

本剧本开始时没有遭遇牌库。这意味着调查员无法以任何方式使用与遭遇牌库互动的能力。（举例来说，搜索遭遇牌库、从遭遇牌库抽卡、查看遭遇牌库中的卡牌等效果都会失败。）

此外，幕 1a 上有这样的文字：「神话阶段期间，不要从遭遇牌库抽卡。」

在本剧本的某个时点，调查员会得到指示去组成遭遇牌库，此后这段文字不再生效。从那时起，调查员可以像平常一样与遭遇牌库互动。

如果没有达成任何结局，因为每名调查员都被击败了：

一只年迈的疤痕猫把你轻轻推醒。「嘿。你还好吗，人类？」

「我在做梦」，你想起这一点，于是会说话的猫突然也没那么古怪了。你筋疲力尽地站起身，拍掉衣服上结块的泥土。「你们运气不错，在我们赶到之前没有受伤。」一个人声朝你喊道。声音属于一个穿着棕色旅行外套的金发男人，他斜靠在附近的一棵树上。「这片森林对胆怯的人可不会留情。」疤痕猫走到男人身边，男人俯身抚摸它的背。

你问男人这里是什么地方、他又怎么会来到此处，却被他打断。「到时候我自会解释。眼下我们必须沿这条路前往乌撒镇。那里算是安全的地方，相对而言。你们可以在那里从磨难中恢复过来。」他转向那只猫，用一种古怪的语言说出一个词——你猜那大概是某种口令——可猫只是朝树篱那边晃过去，你看见还有几只猫聚在那里。「你自己来吧。」它答道。

「别在意那些猫。」猫群离开时，男人低声对你说。「它们是有用的盟友，但也是独立的生灵，并不需要你我。等我们到了乌撒，你也许有机会见到它们其他的同类。不过先办正事要紧。」你们一起离开了魔幻森林的林缘。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「调查员被伦道夫·卡特救下」。

• 任意一名调查员可以选择把伦道夫·卡特（资深入梦者）（《食梦者》第 59 号卡）加入自己的牌库。此卡不计入该调查员的牌库张数。

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 经验：XP

• 如果你以四章战役的形式进行梦寻，前往幕间 I：黑猫。

• 如果你以互联八章战役的形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……并且尚未进行过剧本 1–B：清醒噩梦，前往该剧本。

• ……并且已经进行过剧本 1–B：清醒噩梦，则改为前往幕间 I：黑猫。

那些生物彼此吱吱议论，过了一会儿，其中十几只朝小路之外那棵大树的方向退去。它们很快就回来了，嘴里叼着各种各样的松鸡、鹌鹑和雉鸡。你现在几乎可以肯定自己快疯了。然而，这场奇景仍在继续。那些生物怯生生地把鸟当作「贡品」丢在猫群面前，然后悄悄离去。「我代祖格鼠向你们道歉。」男人走近时说道。「它们是好奇的生灵，平时并不这么……躁动。幸好我们及时赶到。」猫群的首领跳上一个树桩，补充道：「对，对。那些可恶的祖格鼠已经尽了自己的本分，现在轮到我们，离开这个被遗弃的地方吧。你们说呢？」

你压抑不住兴奋。祖格鼠、会说话的猫——你读过的一切都是真的。你开始向男人追问这个世界的更多事情，却被他打断。「到时候我自会解释。眼下我们必须沿这条路前往乌撒镇。那里算是安全的地方，相对而言。你们可以在那里从旅途中恢复过来。」他转向那只年迈的疤痕猫，用一种古怪的语言说出一个词——你猜那大概是某种口令——猫快速点了点头作为回应。其余的猫叼着贡品，在你周围排成护卫的圆阵，你们一起逃出了魔幻森林的林缘。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「猫群收到了祖格鼠的贡品」。

• 任意一名调查员可以选择把伦道夫·卡特（资深入梦者）（《食梦者》第 59 号卡）加入自己的牌库。此卡不计入该调查员的牌库张数。

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 经验：XP

• 如果你以四章战役的形式进行梦寻，前往幕间 I：黑猫。

• 如果你以互联八章战役的形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……并且尚未进行过剧本 1–B：清醒噩梦，前往该剧本。

• ……并且已经进行过剧本 1–B：清醒噩梦，则改为前往幕间 I：黑猫。

你朝这些新来的访客举起一只手，相信自己能独自化解这个局面。要是早知道这些鼠类生物一直都有智慧，你或许会早得多就尝试与它们沟通。你告诉它们，你们只是这片遥远土地上的旅人，只希望能和平地经过。那些生物彼此吱吱议论了一阵：「他们是好人！」「他们果然不是和黑猫一伙的！」「快召唤贤者议会！」过了一会儿，又有好几只出现，每只都长着暗淡的灰色皮毛、身体瘦弱单薄。最年长的那只从你身后探头张望，说只要你能让猫群离开，它们就愿意帮助你。

你勉强压住难以置信的心情，礼貌地请猫群改天再来。「行吧。」疤痕猫回答，「但你最好记住我们，这事没完。」猫群退到森林边缘，不过它们的人类同伴留了下来和你在一起。等猫群走远到听不见的地方，一位长老递给你一只葫芦，里面装的似乎是发酵的树汁，你客气地接了下来。

「这是月树之酒。」你身后的男人走上前，轻声解释道。「祖格鼠不会轻易送出这样的礼物。它们是好奇的生灵，但并非没有智慧。既然你现在可以和它们的长老畅谈，试着问它们一个问题吧。它们对这片土地上的事情了解得比你想象的多。」

你描述了作家维吉尔·格雷，并问祖格鼠是否见过一个符合这副模样的人穿过这片森林。你还补充说，他大概已经走过这条路很多次了。祖格鼠中间安静下来，其中一些立刻钻进茂密的枝叶深处。「我们见过这个人类。」一位长老答道，声音颤颤的，只比耳语响一点。「他常走这条路。他心地不错，但很愚蠢。走上通往乌撒的路吧。你也许能遇见他。」接着它低沉地咕哝道：「……但要提防跟着他的那只猫。所有的猫都爱说谎，黑猫尤其如此。」你谢过那只远古祖格鼠的智慧，随后离开，由金发男人和他的猫护卫带路。你和祖格鼠谈过之后，猫群狐疑地打量着你。男人打破了紧张气氛。「如果你要去乌撒找这位朋友，就让我带你过去。那里算是安全的地方，相对而言。你们可以在那里从旅途中恢复过来。」

祖格鼠。会说话的猫。这一切不可能只是你想象出来的幻象。不知怎的，你能在这满目荒唐之下看见一层真相。不管好坏，祖格鼠议会已经证实了你处境的确凿：幻梦境是真的，而维吉尔·格雷就在这里。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「调查员和祖格鼠谈判」。

• 任意一名调查员可以选择把伦道夫·卡特（资深入梦者）（《食梦者》第 59 号卡）加入自己的牌库。此卡不计入该调查员的牌库张数。

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 经验：XP

• 如果你以四章战役的形式进行梦寻，前往幕间 I：黑猫。

• 如果你以互联八章战役的形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……并且尚未进行过剧本 1–B：清醒噩梦，前往该剧本。

• ……并且已经进行过剧本 1–B：清醒噩梦，则改为前往幕间 I：黑猫。

intro.title: Scenario I–A: Beyond the Gates of Sleep

children.text: In player order, each investigator chooses and reads aloud one of the dream entries below that applies to that investigator. “Neutral” dreams may be chosen by any investigator. Each investigator must choose a different dream, if able. Then, proceed to Setup.

Guardian ([guardian]) dream: You circle a sullen hill shrouded in darkness and steeped in fog that seems to swallow all sound. You don’t know what rests within the hill, but it feels older than this world, and it seems like it is watching you. You dare not turn to face the barrow, yet you know you cannot leave it, so instead you endlessly patrol it. In the surrounding hedgerows, you catch glimpses of twisted shadows darting to and fro, but whenever you turn your torch upon them, they vanish. You begin to run but are frozen by a loud knock from behind you. When you turn, the fog parts, and you finally see the base of the hill, where a heavy door of weathered slate calls to you.
Search your deck for a [guardian] card and play it (paying its cost).

Seeker ([seeker]) dream: You hurry through the halls of a university you barely recognize, cradling several textbooks in your arms as you scurry past other students and faculty members. You don’t know how it is possible that you forgot the date of your exam, but if you don’t arrive soon, you know you will fail the class. Somehow, you don’t even remember the course’s subject matter or its curriculum, even though you know it is the end of the semester. It is not like you to skip class or forget to study. You can hear the other students snickering to themselves as you pass. When you reach the end of the hall, the classroom door looms ominiously before you.
Search your deck for a [seeker] card and play it (paying its cost).

Rogue ([rogue]) dream: You conceal a grin as you examine your cards. Jack of diamonds, queen of spades for the nut straight. Your stack of chips is growing larger with each hand, and this will be no different. Bets fly back and forth until it is just you and the man in the white suit across from you. “Are you sure about this?” he taunts, cradling his fingers. You push all of your chips into the center and reveal your king-high straight. “What a shame.” He tsks, revealing a pair of twos. “It appears you have lost everything.” You protest, pointing to your superior hand, but when you examine it again, it has changed. The figures on the face cards are now monstrous shapes with no eyes, many mouths, and tentacled arms. “9♥-10♣-D♦-C♠-N[auto_fail],” the cards read. You gape in shock as you are carried away from the table and ushered out the door.
Search your deck for a [rogue] card and play it (paying its cost).

Mystic ([mystic]) dream: You traverse an enchanted path full of color and vibrancy. Wisps of light hang in the air, bobbing up and down as you approach. With each step you take, the flora along the path atrophy, following no laws of nature. Flowers once bloomed in your wake; now they shrivel as you pass. Vines wither and die. The wisps mock you for your ignorance, yet you do not slow your pace. As you look upon the fair trees, their leaves begin to fall. The once-green grass is dry, brown, and cracked. But even should the whole forest die, it will be worth reaching the other side. When you do, the trail ends abruptly at an ornate wooden door carved into the trunk of a great redwood.
Search your deck for a [mystic] card and play it (paying its cost).

Survivor ([survivor]) dream: You are fleeing through a dark, cramped hall of vine-covered wood. Something inexplicable chases you through the murk. You are too terrified to turn and look upon your pursuer, but nonetheless you know that if it catches you, it will mean the end of your life. It will pierce your heart, drain your blood, and devour your insides. It is this thought that drives you onward, faster than you have ever run before. You cannot let it reach you. You cannot let it feed. Suddenly, you spot your way out: a sturdy wooden door surrounded by a wall of vines.
Search your deck for a [survivor] card and play it (paying its cost).

Criminal dream: The blare of sirens echoes through the streets behind you. They’re gaining on you. They have always been hot on your heels, and you were always one step ahead...until now. You run down an alleyway, and a bright-red glare follows you. They’re going to catch you. They’ll lock you in a cage and throw away the key. Your freedom, your lifestyle, everything you are, everything you love: they’ll take it all away. And why? Just because you wouldn’t play by their rules? When have they ever gotten everything right? You round a corner just as the bulls are about to catch up to you and spot the entrance into a brick building.
Search your deck for a Criminal or Illicit card and play it (paying its cost).

Drifter dream: You meander through a field of flowers, a warm spring breeze nudging your steps forward. A train track divides the field, and as you meet its parallel lines, the roaring clatter of steam and iron lumbers toward you. As the train passes by, you grab onto a ladder hanging from one of its many rusted and weather-beaten cars. Given the appearance of the exterior, the train’s interior is full of unexpected luxury and affluence: Persian rugs hang as decoration, marble staircases wind to dizzying heights, and a crystal chandelier speckles the room with prismatic brilliance. Under the chandelier sits an ornate doorway, its gilded lattices forming the depiction of a fox in a forest.
You may replace a basic weakness in your deck with a different random basic weakness. If you do, suffer 1 trauma of your choice.

Hunter dream: You stalk your prey through a decrepit house, its halls smelling of mold and dust. The creature you hunt is an abomination from an unnatural world. It threatens humanity’s very existence with its presence. You catch its uncanny shape entering one of the doorways upstairs. It cannot escape now—it is yours. But when you enter its den, you find only a dirty, cracked mirror and your own tired and troubled face reflected in the glass. Where could the aberration have gone? You are sure this is where it retreated to, and yet...you turn back to the entrance and are surprised to see a door where there was none before.
Search your deck for a Weapon card and play it (paying its cost).

Medic or Assistant dream: You stand in front of a closed casket. Mourners in black clothing stand in a line at your side, waiting for you to say your last words. Tearfully, you place a hand on the casket. The hard, cold wood feels dead under your palm. They confided in you. They relied on you. And in their time of utmost need, you failed them. All of this—the cold casket, the mourning friends and family—it is all because of you. But when you open the casket, there is no body inside: only a long stone passageway leading deep underground. Suddenly, one of the mourners pushes you forward, and you fall over the edge of the casket and down into the pit below, landing painfully on your side. As you rise to your feet, you find your only exit: a stone archway leading somewhere else entirely...
Choose another investigator. They begin this scenario with 2 additional resources and 1 additional card in their opening hand.

Miskatonic or Scholar dream: You are in an old, forgotten library, surrounded by the knowledge of the ancients. Hundreds of thousands of tomes line the shelves around you, ascending into an empty void above. The dim halls smell of musty pages and melting wax. Taking one of the thick tomes from a nearby shelf, you begin to read. Although you cannot seem to read any of the words, you are utterly absorbed by the tale the pages weave. Your surroundings fade into triviality as time passes. Nothing matters but the shapes of the crimson ink; all else is meaningless in the face of such stark truths. All around you, the library burns to its foundations. Just as the flames reach you, a door out of the library calls to you. Somehow, it stands unburned among the flames.
Search your deck for a Tome card and play it (paying its cost).

Veteran dream: You are in a muddy, soot-filled trench. All around you, the thunderous din of war rages on and on, never ending. Dead litter the trenches: friends and comrades-in-arms who lost their lives over nothing, in a land far from home. You peer over the rim of the trench and into no-man’s-land, a barren waste of broken, charred countryside where death is certain. And there, you see it: a lone wooden door standing among the rubble and dirt. You know it is your only way out. Gripping your rifle tight, you go over the top and run headlong into a hail of deadly bullets, explosions rocking the ground around you.
Search your deck for up to 2 Tactic and/or Supply cards and begin this scenario with them as additional cards in your opening hand.

Wayfarer dream: You trudge chest-deep through a brackish swamp. Impossibly large bulrushes tower over you, and clouds of strange, iridescent insects swarm through the fetid air. With each step, your feet sink deeper into the soft muck, threatening to pull you under. You feel something slick and cold glide across your leg, and you lunge toward dry land—but the more you struggle, the farther you sink. In the blink of an eye, you are consumed whole by the mire, yet you are still falling ever downward. Eventually, you are deposited onto a stone floor along with a small mudslide. You find yourself in a sealed chamber, lit by the pale- blue glimmering of strange hieroglyphs. The symbols frame an intricate golden door: the door to the crypt you’ve been searching for.
Search your deck for a Wayfarer or Relic card and play it (paying its cost).

Neutral dream: You toss and turn but do not sleep, not even for a moment. Your mind is filled with discomfort and dark thoughts: thoughts of failure, of ineptitude, of loss. Your brow is covered in sweat. No matter how you lie, your bed is either too hot or too cold. Finally, sick of getting nowhere, you rise and head to the sink to splash some water on your face. That is when you realize the layout of your room is not as it was before—and the door to your bathroom has been replaced with a large gateway of onyx and marble.
You begin this scenario with 2 additional resources.

Neutral dream: You sit on the back patio of what seems like your childhood home, but something is off. You don’t recognize your family...the plants in the back yard are arranged differently...and the sky is a patchwork of rotting corpses, raining dismembered body parts onto the landscape. Your not-family watches this precipitation of corpses calmly, discussing the weather it as if it were a banal occurrence. This continues even as the intermittent thudding of hands and feet onto your roof intensifies into a torrent of maimed torsos that causes the ceiling to sag. You run outside, weaving through the deadly rain, and head instinctively toward the edge of your parents’ property. As you hear the crash of the house collapsing behind you, you push away the fallen limbs piling atop an old, familiar spot and are relieved to find the weathered wood of a cellar door.
You begin this scenario with 1 additional card in your opening hand.
Gather all cards from the following encounter sets: Beyond the Gates of Sleep, Agents of Nyarlathotep, Zoogs, Dreamer’s Curse, Dreamlands, and Chilling Cold.
Put the Seventy Steps (Of Lighter Slumber) and The Cavern of Flame into play. Each investigator begins at the Seventy Steps (Of Lighter Slumber).
Set the following cards aside, out of play: Randolph Carter (Expert Dreamer), the Laboring Gug enemy, the two double-sided enemy cards (Nasht and Kaman-Thah), and each of the remaining locations.
Note: Nasht and Kaman-Thah are double-sided and have story cards on their other side. For the best experience, do not look at the other side unless an effect instructs you to do so.

This scenario does not begin with an encounter deck in play. Set all of the remaining encounter cards aside, in a single pile. They will be shuffled together at a later time to form the encounter deck. (See “Steps of Slumber,” below.)

At the start of this scenario, there is no encounter deck. This means that the investigators cannot use abilities that interact with the encounter deck in any way. (For example, effects such as those that search the encounter deck, draw cards from the encounter deck, or look at cards in the encounter deck all fail.)

Additionally, act 1a has the text: “Do not draw cards from the encounter deck during the mythos phase.”

At a certain point in the scenario, the investigators will be instructed to form the encounter deck, and this text will no longer be active. From that point onward, the investigators can interact with the encounter deck as normal.

If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated:

You are nudged into consciousness by an old, scarred cat. “Hey. You all right, human?”

I’m dreaming, you remember, and suddenly the talking cat doesn’t seem quite as weird. Exhausted, you manage to rise to your feet, brushing off the dirt caked on your clothing. “You’re lucky you weren’t harmed before we arrived,” a human voice calls out to you. It belongs to a blond-haired man in a brown traveling coat, who leans against a nearby tree. “These woods are not forgiving to the faint of heart.” The scarred cat walks to the man’s side, and the man leans over to pet its back.

You ask the man where you are and how he came to this place, but he cuts you off. “I will explain in due time. For now, we must follow the path to the town of Ulthar. It is a safe place, relatively speaking. There you may recover from your ordeals.” He turns to the cat and utters a word in an odd language—a password of sorts, you suspect—but the cat simply wanders off toward a hedge, where you see several other cats banded together. “Do it yerself,” it replies.

“Don’t mind the cats,” the man says to you quietly as the cats depart. “They are useful allies, but also independent creatures with no need for you or me. When we reach Ulthar, you may get the chance to meet others of their kind. But first things first.” Together, you leave the eaves of the enchanted forest behind.

• In your Campaign Log, record the investigators were saved by Randolph Carter.

• Any one investigator may choose to add Randolph Carter (Expert Dreamer) (The Dream-Eaters card #59) to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator’s deck size.

• Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.
• Experience: (calculate as instructed above)

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest as a four-part campaign, proceed to Interlude I: The Black Cat.

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest and The Web of Dreams as an interconnected eight-part campaign…
• …and you have not yet played Scenario 1–B: Waking Nightmare, proceed to that scenario.

• …and you have already played Scenario 1–B: Waking Nightmare, proceed instead to Interlude I: The Black Cat.

The creatures chitter among themselves, and after a moment, a dozen of them retreat in the direction of the great tree beyond the beaten path. They return shortly afterward carrying a variety of grouse, quail, and pheasants in their mouths. You’re almost certain now that you are going crazy. And yet, the spectacle continues. The creatures timidly drop their “tribute” of birds in front of the cats and quietly depart. “My apologies on behalf of the Zoogs,” the man says as he approaches. “They are curious creatures, and not usually so...agitated. It is good that we showed up when we did.” The leader of the cats jumps on a tree stump and adds, “Yes, yes. Them vile Zoogs have done their part, now let’s do ours and leave this forsaken place. What say yeh?”

You cannot contain your excitement. Zoogs, talking cats— everything you have read about is real. You begin to ask the man more about this world, but he cuts you off. “I will explain in due time. For now, we must follow the path to the town of Ulthar. It is a safe place, relatively speaking. There you may recover from your travels.” He turns to the old, scarred cat and utters a word in an odd language—a password of sorts, you suspect—and the cat replies with a quick nod. The rest of the cats, tribute in mouth, take a protective circular formation around you, and together you escape from the eaves of the enchanted forest.

• In your Campaign Log, record the cats collected their tribute from the Zoogs.

• Any one investigator may choose to add Randolph Carter (Expert Dreamer) (The Dream-Eaters card #59) to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator’s deck size.

• Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.
• Experience: (calculate as instructed above)

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest as a four-part campaign, proceed to Interlude I: The Black Cat.

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest and The Web of Dreams as an interconnected eight-part campaign…
• …and you have not yet played Scenario 1–B: Waking Nightmare, proceed to that scenario.

• …and you have already played Scenario 1–B: Waking Nightmare, proceed instead to Interlude I: The Black Cat.

You hold a hand up to the new visitors, believing that you can defuse this situation on your own. Had you known these rodent-like creatures were intelligent all along, you might have tried to communicate with them much earlier. You inform them that you are just travelers in this faraway land and that you simply wish to pass through peacefully. The creatures chitter among themselves for a moment: “They are kind!” “They are not with the black cat after all!” “Summon the Council of Sages!” After a short while, several more of them appear, each with withering grey fur and a frail, thin body. The eldest one peeks behind you and states that they will aid you if you get the cats to leave.

Somehow, you contain your disbelief and politely ask the cats to come back another time. “All right,” the scarred cat replies, “but you ain’t seen the last of us.” The cats retreat to the edge of the woods, though their human companion stays behind with you. Once the cats are out of earshot, one of the elders offers you a gourd of what appears to be fermented tree sap, which you accept graciously.

“It is the wine of the moon-tree,” the man behind you explains quietly, stepping forward. “The Zoogs do not give such gifts lightly. They are curious creatures, but not without wisdom. Now that you may speak freely with their elders, try asking them a question. They know more of the dealings of this land than you might think.”

You describe the author Virgil Gray and ask the Zoogs if they have seen a man fitting that description pass through these woods. You add that he would have walked this path many times. A hush falls over the Zoogs, and some of them immediately depart into the deep foliage. “We have met this human,” one of the elders replies with a flutter just louder than a whisper. “He often comes this way. He is kind but foolish. Take the road to Ulthar. You may meet him.” Then it adds with a low growl: “...but beware the cat that follows him. All cats are liars, but the black cat especially.” You thank the ancient Zoog for its wisdom and depart, led by the blond man and his feline escort. The cats eye you suspiciously after your discussion with the Zoogs. The man breaks the tension. “If you are heading to Ulthar to find this friend of yours, allow me to guide you there. It is a safe place, relatively speaking. There you may recover from your travels.”

Zoogs. Talking cats. This can’t all be a figment of your imagination. Somehow, you can see a layer of truth beneath all of this absurdity. For better or for worse, the Zoog council has confirmed the reality of your situation: the Dreamlands are real, and Virgil Gray is here.

• In your Campaign Log, record the investigators parleyed with the Zoogs.

• Any one investigator may choose to add Randolph Carter (Expert Dreamer) (The Dream-Eaters card #59) to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator’s deck size.

• Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.
